title: Flesh and Blood: Learn to Play

sections.title: The goal
sections.summary: Flesh and Blood is a head-to-head game built around the heroes. Win by reducing your opponent's life to zero.
points: Your hero begins in the arena and is the focus of the fight.
Cards, equipment, and weapons help you attack, defend, and manage resources.

sections.title: Game zones
sections.summary: Cards move between named zones as the game progresses. The arena is the hero, weapons, equipment, combat chain, and other permanents in play.
points: The deck is face-down; the hand is drawn from it. Pitch holds cards used to generate resources.
The arsenal stores one face-down card for a future turn. The graveyard holds resolved, discarded, or destroyed cards; banished cards go to the banished zone.
Attacks and defending cards meet on the combat chain. Weapons and equipment return to their zones after combat.

sections.title: Getting ready
sections.summary: Set up your hero, equipment, and deck before drawing your opening hand.
points: Place your hero face-up, decide who goes first, and choose your weapons and equipment before seeing the opponent's choices.
Choose a legal deck for the format, shuffle it, and let the opponent cut it. Reveal your weapons and equipment, then draw cards up to your hero's intellect.
There is no mulligan: the cards you draw are your starting hand.

sections.title: Turn structure
sections.summary: Each turn moves through the start phase, action phase, and end phase.
points: Start: resolve effects that happen at the beginning of the turn.
Action: begin with one action point. Playing an action with go again returns an action point when it resolves.
End: you may put a card from hand into an empty arsenal, return pitched cards to the bottom of the deck, lose unused points, and draw back up to intellect.

sections.title: Playing a card
sections.summary: Announce the card and any targets or modes, then pay every cost before it resolves.
points: Pitch cards from your hand to gain resource points equal to their pitch value. You may pitch only as much as needed to cover the resource cost.
Pay additional costs after the resource cost. If you cannot pay all costs, you cannot play the card.
Action cards use an action point. Any unspent resources remain available for the rest of your turn.

sections.title: Activating abilities
sections.summary: To activate an ability, announce it, pay its costs, and resolve its effect, much like playing a card.
points: Abilities are written as limit, type, cost, and effect. A limit such as once per turn restricts how often it can be used.
Action abilities require an action point; instants can be used at other times, and reactions are used during combat's reaction step.
An ability whose effect is an attack starts combat.

sections.title: Combat
sections.summary: An attack resolves as a chain link. Finish its steps before playing another action.
points: Layer: play or activate the attack and choose its target. Attack: it moves onto the combat chain and attacks with its power.
Defend: the defender may use eligible equipment and cards from hand. Compare total defense with attack power; excess power becomes damage, and damage means the attack hit.
Reaction: players may play attack or defense reactions. Then resolve damage and hit effects, and continue the chain or end combat.

sections.title: Closing combat
sections.summary: At the close step, clear the combat chain and return cards to their proper zones.
points: Weapons and equipment return to their respective zones.
Other cards remaining on the combat chain go to their owners' graveyards.

sections.title: The golden rule
sections.summary: When a card's instructions contradict a general game rule, follow the card text.
points: A card may grant permission to do something the rules normally prohibit; follow that specific instruction.
